$comment: United States baseline binding, as of 2026-10-27. Authored priors, not fitted: every number is a judgement anchored to the instrument catalogue in ../instruments.json and carries its basis inline. Shares are of the reference firm's in-scope annual AI revenue.

frontier.basis: Frontier-developer transparency + incident reporting. Coverage ~half of US AI revenue sits with the handful of >1e26-FLOP / >$500M-revenue developers. Cost is framework publication and reporting, not capability restriction. p_in_force 0.75: SB 53 has applied since 2026-01-01 but is an obvious DOJ AI Litigation Task Force target and the Obernolte-Trahan draft would preempt it.

highrisk.basis: Consequential-decision / algorithmic-discrimination duties (impact assessments, notices, appeal). p_in_force 0.45 is the contested core of the US regime: Colorado's AG agreed in April 2026 not to enforce until interpretive rulemaking that has not started, the US intervened in xAI v. Weiser, and a replacement framework is pending.

filing.basis: The US has no general ex-ante gate. Only sectoral pre-market review (FDA AI-enabled device software, similar FAA/NHTSA paths) gates launch; coverage is that sliver of AI revenue.

content.basis: Takedown, provenance and companion-chatbot duties. TAKE IT DOWN Act notice-and-removal obligations apply to platforms; California provenance/disclosure and companion-chatbot statutes add state layers; the EO 14365 carve-out leaves child-safety laws outside the preemption push, so p_in_force is high.

data.basis: No federal privacy statute; ~20 state comprehensive privacy laws, FTC Section 5 enforcement on AI claims and data practices, and the DOJ bulk-sensitive-data rule restricting transfers to countries of concern.

trade.basis: Outbound export controls as borne by US AI firms: coverage is the chip/systems share of US AI revenue; cost_share is licensing overhead plus forgone China sales. Blackwell-class denied; H200/MI325X case-by-case since 2026-01-15 under a 50%-of-US-volume cap and a 25% Section 232 tariff; May 2026 guidance extends licensing to China-parented entities abroad.

fragmentation.basis: Distinct regimes a national deployer must map (federal + ~11 states with material AI-specific duties). Fixed legal/program cost per regime per year for the reference firm. The patchwork is the US cost driver the preemption fight is about.

reference_firm.basis: Mid-size AI application/model firm; fixed costs are regressive, so a larger firm sees a smaller fixed_burden.

ex_ante_gate.basis: Sectoral pre-market review runs ~6 months. obsolescence_per_year is the share of a model/product's annual value lost to a year of delay in a market where frontier capability turns over roughly annually.

state_support.basis: Federal support netted against burden: CHIPS-era incentives, federal compute access programs, permitting acceleration for data centres under the AI Action Plan. Small relative to revenue.

compute.basis: US firms face no import licensing for frontier accelerators; access is bounded by supply chain, not regulation. Treated as fully accessible.
